verdicts.evidence: 3200 numpy instances across n_out, m, rank-deficiency, and p-norm grid show 0 violations of the bound ||P*−f_t||_p < (3+3√n_out)K, with mutation tests (violating the w_phi norm premise or replacing argmin with argmax) producing hundreds of violations, confirming the bound depends on the stated hypotheses.

280 instances confirm that the null-space term (I−A_g^+A_g)w_phi preserves sub-constraint satisfaction (max violation 1.8e-13), spans the entire feasible set on each face (reachability error 1.7e-14), reduces to fixed orthogonal projection when w_phi=0, and improves loss on 76.3% of optimization instances; mutation removing the term eliminates all gains.

27,900 exhaustive cases (E1) and 8,800 random cases (E2) including 1,275 rank-deficient systems show 0 CAffNet feasibility failures, while HardNet's single pseudo-inverse correction fails in 59.2%–77.3% of cases; cardinality formula |Γ|=Σ C(m,k) for k≤min(m,n_out) verified, and truncating to k≤min(m,n_out)−1 causes 24%+ failures.

CPU-scale run with 8000 epochs (paper: 50000) and 5 seeds yields 75.58% MSE reduction (paper: 73.33%) with 0 CAffNet-TF violations and 26% soft-NN violations—results closely match but the training setup is clearly reduced in epochs and hardware.

Reduced-scale run (20 vs 300 initial states, 60 epochs, 3 seeds, CPU) shows CAffNet with 0 collisions and Soft NN with 3 collisions, but HardNet also has 0 collisions (contradicting the claim that HardNet fails to avoid obstacles), though HardNet does exhibit 1.70 mean test violations; the very reduced state space limits definitive conclusions.

overall: The logbook provides strong numerical verification for the three theoretical claims (Theorem 3.5 bound, trainable null-space component, rank-deficiency handling) through exhaustive grid testing and mutation controls. The two experimental claims are addressed only at reduced scale (CPU, fewer epochs/states), with Claim 4 closely matching paper numbers but Claim 5 partially contradicting the paper on HardNet's collision behavior.
